# Restful Booker API Testing

This collection contains manual API tests and automated Postman assertions created while learning REST API testing using the Restful Booker API.

The project follows a sprint-based approach, where each sprint focuses on a specific API module and includes planning, implementation, execution, documentation, and version control.

## Objectives

- Learn REST API fundamentals
    
- Practice API testing using Postman
    
- Create reusable requests and environments
    
- Validate API responses with automated assertions
    
- Document professional QA artifacts
    
- Build a portfolio demonstrating real QA workflows
    

## Sprint Structure

- Sprint 01 – Health Check
    
- Sprint 02 – Authentication
    
- Sprint 03 – Retrieve Booking IDs
    
- Sprint 04 – Retrieve Booking by ID
    
- Sprint 05 – Create Booking
    
- Sprint 06 – Update Booking
    
- Sprint 07 – Partial Update Booking
    
- Sprint 08 – Delete Booking
    
- Sprint 09 – End-to-End Workflow
    

## Tools

- Postman
    
- JavaScript
    
- Git
    
- GitHub
    
- Newman (planned)
    
- GitHub Actions (planned)
    

This collection is part of my QA Portfolio and is maintained using Git version control.

# Sprint 01 – Health Check

## Sprint Goal

The goal of this sprint is to verify that the Restful Booker API is available and responding correctly before testing any business functionality.

The `/ping` endpoint serves as the application's health check and provides a quick way to confirm that the API is operational.

---

## Learning Objectives

During this sprint I will learn:

- REST API fundamentals
    
- HTTP request and response lifecycle
    
- GET requests
    
- Postman Collections
    
- Postman Environments
    
- Environment Variables
    
- Writing JavaScript assertions
    
- Executing API requests
    
- Recording execution results
    
- Using Git for version control
    

---

## Scope

**Endpoint**

```
GET /ping

 ```

**Method**

```
GET

 ```

---

## Test Scenarios

- Verify API availability
    
- Verify response contract
    
- Verify unsupported HTTP methods
    
- Verify endpoint response performance
    

---

## Expected Deliverables

- Postman request
    
- Automated Postman tests
    
- Execution evidence
    
- Updated documentation
    
- Git commit
    
- GitHub push
    

---

| --- | --- |
| Learn endpoint | ✅ |

| Capture Evidence | ✅ |

# Sprint 02 – Authentication

## Sprint Goal

The goal of this sprint is to verify that the Restful Booker API correctly authenticates users and generates an authentication token for valid credentials before testing protected endpoints.

The **/auth** endpoint is responsible for issuing authentication tokens, which are required to perform authorized operations such as updating and deleting bookings.

---

## Learning Objectives

During this sprint I will learn:

- POST requests
    
- JSON Request Body
    
- Authentication vs Authorization
    
- Authentication Tokens
    
- Environment Variables
    
- Request Body Validation
    
- Positive API Testing
    
- Negative API Testing
    
- Boundary Value Analysis
    
- API Contract Validation
    
- HTTP Headers
    
- Basic API Security Testing
    
- Writing JavaScript assertions
    
- Recording execution results
    
- Using Git for version control
    

---

## Scope

### Endpoint

``` text
POST /auth

 ```

### Method

``` text
POST

 ```

---

## Test Scenarios

- Verify successful authentication using valid credentials
    
- Verify authentication fails with invalid credentials
    
- Verify required authentication fields
    
- Verify authentication request data type validation
    
- Verify authentication request boundary values
    
- Verify authentication response contract
    
- Verify authentication request headers
    
- Verify authentication security behavior
    

---

## Expected Deliverables

- Postman request
    
- Automated Postman tests
    
- Authentication token
    
- Execution evidence
    
- Updated documentation
    
- Git commit
    
- GitHub push
    

---

## Sprint Status

| Task | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Learn Authentication endpoint | ✅ |
| Configure Environment Variables | ✅ |
| Build Request Body | ✅ |
| Build Request | ✅ |
| Write Tests | ✅ |
| Execute Positive Request | ✅ |
| Execute Negative Requests | ✅ |
| Store Authentication Token | ✅ |
| Capture Evidence | ✅ |
| Update Documentation | ✅ |
| Git Commit | ✅ |
| GitHub Push | ✅ |

---

## Notes

Sprint 02 introduces authentication, one of the fundamental concepts in API testing.

The authentication token generated during this sprint will be stored as an environment variable and reused throughout the remaining sprints when testing protected API endpoints.

This sprint also introduces request body validation, boundary value analysis, response contract validation and basic security testing, establishing the foundation for authenticated CRUD operations later in the project.
